mainTopic: Purifying pressing baskets and the length of an עונה; a bride's bleeding after the בעילת מצוה; telling נדה blood from בתולים blood
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about getting olive and grape pressing baskets ready for use in purity. Less absorbent baskets are washed, while absorbent ones must sit unused for twelve months, or from one pressing season to the next. רבי יוסי gives faster methods: boiling water, hot olive water, or leaving them in running water for an עונה. The גמרא fixes the wording of the comparison to יין נסך, and then shows that an עונה is twelve hours in every season. Next comes the practical ruling of רב and שמואל: a groom completes the בעילת מצוה and then separates. This ruling is challenged from the משנה and from a story about רבי. The answer is that it follows a later vote of רבותינו, and רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש ruled the same way. A ברייתא then explains that bleeding which continues past the bride's allowed nights must be checked. רבי מאיר says the two kinds of blood can be told apart by their appearance, while the חכמים say all blood looks the same. The amud ends with a new ברייתא about a woman who bleeds from marital relations three times.

steps.title: Washing or resting the pressing baskets
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that palm and hemp baskets are washed, while bast and reed baskets must be left unused for twelve months. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says from one pressing season to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Baskets made of palm leaves or hemp: you clean them. Baskets made of bast or reeds: you leave them unused. How long? Twelve months. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: leave them from one wine-pressing to the next, or from one olive-pressing to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us how to get pressing baskets ready, based on what material they are made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baskets made of palm leaves or hemp absorb less, so washing them is enough. Baskets made of bast or reeds soak up more liquid, so they must sit unused until what they absorbed is gone. The תנא קמא sets this at twelve months, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל measures it by pressing seasons instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Woven baskets or bags used to hold olives or grapes in the press
He lets them 'get old', meaning he leaves them unused for a while

phrases.aramaic: הָעֲקָלִים שֶׁל נְצָרִים וְשֶׁל בִּצְבּוּץ — מְנַגְּבָן,
phrases.english: The baskets of palm leaves or of hemp: he cleans them.
Those of bast or of reeds: he leaves them unused.
And how long does he leave them? Twelve months.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He leaves them from wine-pressing to wine-pressing, and from olive-pressing to olive-pressing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא already being quoted on the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Absorbent baskets (bast, reeds) must sit unused for twelve months. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says from one pressing season to the next.

steps.title: Isn't that the same as the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differs from the תנא קמא, since one season to the next is twelve months anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as the first תנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops quoting the ברייתא to ask a question: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to be saying exactly what the תנא קמא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From one wine-pressing season to the next is about a year. So 'season to season' and 'twelve months' look like the same rule, and there seems to be no real argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: That is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second opinion in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'from press to press'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One pressing season to the next is twelve months, so the two opinions look the same.

steps.title: The difference: early and late ripening
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is the early and late ripening seasons, so season to season is not always exactly twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is early and late ripening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions do differ, because harvest seasons can come early or late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא needs exactly twelve months. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only needs one season to the next, which can be a little more or a little less than a year depending on when the fruit ripens. So the two opinions give different results in early or late years.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a practical difference between them

phrases.english: The difference between them is early and late ripening.
phrases.notes: A season can come a bit sooner or later than exactly a year after the last one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Season to season is always exactly twelve months, so the opinions are the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seasons vary, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a period that is not exactly twelve months.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא counts exact months. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל counts by harvest seasons, which may be slightly more or less than a year.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's quick methods: boiling water or olive water
steps.stepSummary: Back in the ברייתא, רבי יוסי says that someone who wants the baskets pure right away can purge them in boiling water or scald them in olive water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Someone who wants to purify them right away purges them in boiling water or scalds them in olive water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא. רבי יוסי offers a way to avoid waiting twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of waiting for what was absorbed to dry out, hot water or hot olive water pushes it out right away. This is a shortcut for someone in a hurry.

keyTerms.meaning: He purges them in boiling water (like הגעלה)
Olive water, the hot liquid from olives

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
One who wishes to purify them immediately,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the absorbent baskets, so he won't have to wait the twelve months.

phrases.english: purges them in boiling water
or scalds them in olive water.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הָרוֹצֶה לְטַהֵר מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא after the short discussion in steps 2 and 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hot water or hot olive water purifies the baskets immediately.

steps.title: Another method: running water
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, in the name of רבי יוסי, says to place the baskets under a flowing pipe or in a fast-moving spring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי יוסי: He puts them under a pipe whose water keeps flowing, or in a spring whose water runs fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second version of רבי יוסי's view, using cold running water instead of hot water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the method is water that keeps moving and washes the baskets out over time. It is gentler than boiling, so the next step tells us how long it takes.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
He places them under a pipe whose water flows constantly,
or in a spring whose water runs fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רבי יוסי's quick method
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Running water from a pipe or a fast spring can also purify the baskets.

steps.title: How long in the water: an עונה, like יין נסך
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the baskets stay in the running water for an עונה and compares this to what was said about יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for how long? An עונה. The way they said it about יין נסך, that is how they said it about טהרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets the time for the running-water method and links it to the same rule for יין נסך. This line is the setup for the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The time needed is an עונה, a set period. The ברייתא says this matches the rule about baskets used with יין נסך, so the same measure works in both areas. The order of the comparison is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured for עבודה זרה, which is forbidden

phrases.english: And how long? A period.
In the way that they said regarding libation wine,
so they said regarding matters of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה עוֹנָה? כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the running-water rule with a time measure and a comparison
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The baskets stay in running water for an עונה, the same as in יין נסך.

steps.title: The comparison is backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the comparison is upside down, since this ברייתא is about טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's the other way around! We are dealing with טהרות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you compare the topic you are discussing to some other topic: 'just as there, so here.' Since this ברייתא is about טהרות, it should not present טהרות as the side that copies יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: Toward the other side, meaning 'that's backwards!'

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not arguing about the halacha. It only objects to which topic is presented as the main one in the comparison.

phrases.english: Isn't it the opposite?!
We are dealing with matters of purity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the comparison in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'as they said regarding יין נסך, so they said regarding טהרות'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's topic is טהרות, so טהרות should be the main case, not the one being compared to יין נסך.

steps.title: Reading the comparison the right way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the ברייתא: as they said about טהרות, so they said about יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: The way they said it about טהרות, that is how they said it about יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording so the comparison goes in the right direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of an עונה in running water belongs first to טהרות, the topic of this ברייתא. The ברייתא then adds that the same measure applies to יין נסך. The halacha stays the same; only the order of the comparison changes.
steps.whatToRemember: Hot water, olive water, or an עונה in running water can replace the twelve-month wait. The same time measure is shared by טהרות and יין נסך, with טהרות as the main case here.

phrases.english: Rather: in the way that they said regarding matters of purity,
so they said regarding libation wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 7 by reversing the comparison
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא presents יין נסך as the main case and טהרות as the case compared to it.
steps.terutzMaskana: טהרות is the main case, and the same measure is applied to יין נסך.

steps.title: How long is an עונה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much time the עונה in the ברייתא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is an עונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא said the baskets stay in running water for an עונה, so the גמרא now asks how long that is. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עונה means a stretch of time, but its exact length is not obvious. Once we know the length, we know how long the baskets must stay in the water.

phrases.english: And how long is an עונה?
phrases.notes: This is the עונה from the ברייתא, the time the baskets stay in running water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the wording of the ברייתא, the גמרא now defines a term inside it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of time called an עונה.

steps.title: First report: a day or a night
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, as quoted by רבי חייא בר אבא, says an עונה is either a day or a night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: either a day or a night.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: an עונה is one full day or one full night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this report, an עונה is the length of one daytime or one nighttime. So the baskets could go in at dawn and come out at nightfall, or go in at nightfall and come out at dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: Either a day or a night

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Either a day or a night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how long an עונה is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עונה is a full day or a full night.

steps.title: Second report: half a day and half a night
steps.stepSummary: A different chain of students reports that רבי יוחנן said an עונה is half a day and half a night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנה שאונא (some say רבי חנה בר שאונא) said in the name of רבה בר בר חנה, in the name of רבי יוחנן: half a day and half a night.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of רבי יוחנן's words gives a different-sounding answer: half a day plus half a night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there seem to be two different versions of what רבי יוחנן said. One says a whole day or a whole night, and the other says half of each. This sets up the question of whether they really disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a day and half a night

phrases.english: Rabbi Chana She'una,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי חָנָה בַּר שְׁאוּנָא,
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Chana bar She'una,
said that Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Half a day and half a night.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָנָה שְׁאוּנָא וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי חָנָה בַּר שְׁאוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second report of רבי יוחנן's answer that seems to clash with the first.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עונה is half a day plus half a night.

steps.title: Both reports mean twelve hours, depending on the season
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק says the two reports agree: 'a day or a night' is for ניסן and תשרי, and 'half and half' is for תמוז and טבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: They do not disagree. This one is in the season of ניסן and תשרי, and that one is in the season of תמוז and טבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק shows that the two reports do not really argue. Each one describes the same length of time in a different season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ניסן and תשרי, day and night are equal, so a day or a night is twelve hours. In תמוז the day is long and in טבת the night is long, so half a day plus half a night also comes to twelve hours. Either way, an עונה is twelve hours.

keyTerms.meaning: The spring and fall seasons, when day and night are equal
The summer and winter seasons, with the longest day or longest night

steps.whatToRemember: An עונה is always twelve hours. 'A day or a night' and 'half a day and half a night' are two ways of saying it in different seasons.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one report says twelve hours and the other says something longer. Both equal twelve hours. They just describe different seasons.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: And Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
And they do not disagree —
this one is in the season of Nisan and Tishrei,
phrases.notes: This is 'a day or a night.' In these months day and night are each twelve hours.

phrases.english: that one is in the season of Tammuz and Tevet.
phrases.notes: This is 'half and half.' A long day or a long night split in half still adds up to twelve hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent clash between the two reports of רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two reports of רבי יוחנן give different lengths for an עונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both describe twelve hours, each fitting a different season.

steps.title: Reading רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as 'half and half' too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that in the case of the bride's bleeding, the time limit should also be read as half a day and half a night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, say that regarding the bleeding woman it means half a day and half a night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to fit רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's earlier ruling about a new bride into the same twelve-hour pattern. It suggests reading his time limit as 'half a day and half a night.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל had said a new bride can blame her bleeding on the wedding wound for 'a night and half a day,' which sounds longer than twelve hours. To match the twelve-hour עונה, the גמרא proposes that he also meant half a day and half a night. The very next step will challenge this.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman made impure by uterine bleeding; here the bride's bleeding case

phrases.english: Here too,
say that regarding the bleeding woman
phrases.notes: This points back to the case of the new bride whose bleeding may be blamed on her wedding wound.

phrases.english: it is half a day and half a night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves an unstated contradiction: the twelve-hour עונה of step 12 seems to clash with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'a night and half a day' for the bride, so the גמרא proposes rereading his words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the earlier ruling to match
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's time for the bride is longer than an עונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps he too meant half a day and half a night, which equals twelve hours.

steps.title: But he said 'a night and half a day'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל clearly said 'a night and half a day,' not 'half a day and half a night.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'a night and half a day'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion just made. His actual words were 'a night and half a day,' so we can't simply change them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full night plus half a day is not the same as half a night plus half a day. The suggested reading does not match his words, so a better explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A night and half a day

phrases.english: But he said 'a night and half a day'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested reading in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposal that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant half a day and half a night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His words were 'a night and half a day,' which does not fit the suggested reading.

steps.title: Either a night or half and half, depending on the season
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant either a night in ניסן and תשרי or half a day and half a night in טבת and תמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: either a night of ניסן and תשרי, or half a day and half a night of טבת and תמוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading. His words name two options that each fit a different season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A night' means a twelve-hour night in ניסן or תשרי. 'Half a day' (with half a night) is the option for טבת or תמוז. Both options equal twelve hours, so his ruling matches the עונה after all.

phrases.english: Rather:
either a night of Nisan and Tishrei,
or half a day and half a night
of Tevet and Tammuz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14 with a better reading of his words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the words as two seasonal options
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A night and half a day' means one long stretch, longer than twelve hours.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means either a night (ניסן and תשרי) or half a day and half a night (טבת and תמוז), always twelve hours.

steps.title: Second answer: the wedding case is different because of the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the bride's case really is longer, because people take extra time before signing the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: the כתובה is different, because people delay over it a lot until they sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different answer. The bride's case really does have a longer time, and it gives a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words mean exactly what they say: a full night plus half a day. The wedding is different from the baskets because people take a long time before they finish and sign the כתובה. So the חכמים gave this case more time than a regular twelve-hour עונה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces a second answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: (1) רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also meant twelve hours, split by season; or (2) the wedding case is longer because the כתובה signing takes extra time.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
the marriage contract is different —
phrases.notes: He means the wedding case is different from the baskets, because of the כתובה.

phrases.english: since they delay over it a lot,
until they sign it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer instead of the seasonal reading in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (different reason, different time)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every time limit must match the twelve-hour עונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wedding case really is longer, because the כתובה signing is often delayed.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: complete the first act, then separate
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל both rule that the husband performs the בעילת מצוה and then separates from his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: the הלכה is that he performs the מצוה act of relations, and then separates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling from רב and שמואל. Even though the משנה gave the bride extra time, in practice the husband must separate right after the first act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed blood seen during a set period to be blamed on the bride's virginity. רב and שמואל are stricter. After the first act the husband stays away from her, and they do not rely on that extra time.

keyTerms.meaning: The first act of relations that completes the marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for a bride after the first act, and the rest of this section tests it.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
The halakha is: he engages in the relations of מצוה,
and then separates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the time limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the בעילת מצוה, the husband separates from his wife.

steps.title: רב חסדא challenges them from a story about רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא cites a story in which רבי gave a bride four nights within twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: There was a story, and רבי gave her four nights within twelve months!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the ruling of רב and שמואל. He cites a real case in which רבי allowed a bride four nights, not just one act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי let her have four nights, then the husband clearly does not have to separate after the first act. That contradicts רב and שמואל directly.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda raised an objection:
There was an incident, and Rabbi gave her
four nights
within twelve months!
phrases.notes: So רבי let blood over four nights count as from her virginity, which is more than just one act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רב and שמואל that he separates right after the first act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי himself allowed four nights, so the husband does not have to separate right away.

steps.title: רבא asks why רב חסדא did not just use the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why רב חסדא searched for a ברייתא when the משנה itself already contradicts רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Why do I need to search for a refutation? Raise the objection from our משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not disagree that רב and שמואל have a problem. He asks why רב חסדא went looking for an outside source when the משנה itself already gives the bride several nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly gives a bride extra time in which blood is blamed on her virginity. That alone already clashes with רב and שמואל. So the question is about method: why bring a weaker, less-known source?

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Why do I need to go searching for a refutation?
Raise the objection from our mishna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice of source used in the objection in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חסדא used a ברייתא instead of the משנה

steps.title: A real case carries more weight
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא preferred the ברייתא because it records an actual ruling, and a real case teaches more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: a real incident is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב חסדא chose the story. In his view, a ruling a sage actually gave in practice is stronger proof than a general teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה states the law in theory. A מעשה shows a great sage relying on that law in a real case. That makes the challenge to רב and שמואל sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case teaches more than theory

phrases.english: He holds:
A practical incident is greater.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא preferred the ברייתא because it records a real ruling, and a real case is stronger proof.

steps.title: Either way, רב and שמואל still have a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main point: whatever the source, the challenge against רב and שמואל remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, this is difficult for רב and שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside the side question about which source to use. It states that the objection against רב and שמואל still stands and needs an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the משנה and the story of רבי allow more than one act. So רב and שמואל's ruling still seems to go against the sources, and the next step will answer this.

phrases.english: In any case,
it is difficult for Rav and Shmuel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side question in steps 19–20 to the main objection in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רב and שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה and רבי's ruling both allow more than one act, against רב and שמואל.

steps.title: רב and שמואל followed the later vote of רבותינו
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל followed a ברייתא in which 'רבותינו' voted again and decided that the husband performs the first act and separates.
steps.simpleTranslation: They acted like רבותינו, as it was taught in a ברייתא: רבותינו went back and voted that he performs the מצוה act and separates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב and שמואל were not making up a new rule. They followed a later decision by the sages, who voted to be strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and the story of רבי reflect the earlier law. Later the sages reconsidered and voted to require separation after the first act. רב and שמואל ruled according to that later vote, so the challenge is resolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Our Sages, the court that held the later vote

steps.whatToRemember: The final practical הלכה is that the husband performs the בעילת מצוה and then separates. This follows a later vote of רבותינו that was stricter than the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not being rejected as wrong. The sages later voted to be stricter in practice, and רב and שמואל follow that later decision.

phrases.english: They acted in accordance with our Sages,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Our Sages returned and were counted again —
phrases.notes: 'Were counted' means they took a vote.

phrases.english: he engages in the relations of מצוה and separates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty restated in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a later authority that supports the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and שמואל go against the משנה and רבי's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב and שמואל follow the later vote of רבותינו, who required separation after the first act.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש also ruled that the groom acts and separates
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש got almost nothing practical out of the משנה about the young girl. They concluded that the groom performs the בעילת מצוה and then separates.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: When רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש were dealing with the topic of the young girl, they took from it only as much as a fox takes up from a plowed field. They ended their discussion this way: the groom performs the מצוה act and then separates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings עולא's report to show that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש reached the same ruling as רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 the ruling 'he acts and separates' rested on a ברייתא where רבותינו voted again. Now two more major אמוראים are shown holding the same practical ruling. This means they did not follow the משנה's allowance of several nights in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl. Here it means the bride discussed in the משנה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling, that the groom separates right after the first act, becomes the accepted practical law, even though the משנה gives more time.

phrases.english: Ulla said: When they were engaged in it,
Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish, with the topic of the young girl,
phrases.notes: This is the girl from the משנה who sees blood after her wedding night.

phrases.english: they did not bring up from it
except as much as a fox brings up from a plowed field,
phrases.notes: In other words, they got almost nothing out of it. They did not rule like the משנה.

phrases.english: and they concluded it this way:
He performs the מצוה act of relations and separates.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר עולא כי הוו בה רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש בתינוקת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש for the ruling of רב and שמואל given in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the groom performs the בעילת מצוה and then separates
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's report of how רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש concluded their discussion

steps.title: Should a pious man not finish the act at all?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges רב אשי: if the groom must separate, then a pious man should not even complete the act, so that he does not continue too long.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רב אשי: If that is so, a pious person should not complete his act of relations!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא pushes the new ruling further and asks whether it leads to an even stricter result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood after the first act may be forbidden blood, then continuing to the end might already be a problem. So a truly careful man should stop before finishing. רבי אבא asks why the חכמים did not require that.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If that is so.' It opens a challenge that takes an idea to its logical end.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi:
If that is so,
a pious person should not complete his act of relations!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לו רבי אבא לרב אשי אלא מעתה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'acts and separates' ruling by asking why it does not go further.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the groom performs the בעילת מצוה and then separates
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he must separate because of blood, a careful man should not even finish the act, so that he does not continue longer than allowed.

steps.title: Too much fear would keep him away completely
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that such a rule would make the groom so afraid that he would stay away and never complete the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, his heart will strike him with fear, and he will separate completely.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the חכמים did not make the stricter rule רבי אבא suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule telling the groom not to finish would fill him with worry about bleeding during the act. Then he would avoid his wife altogether, and the מצוה would not be done. So the חכמים stopped at 'acts and separates.'

keyTerms.meaning: His heart strikes him, meaning he is gripped by worry

steps.whatToRemember: The law is that the groom completes the בעילת מצוה and then separates. The חכמים did not go stricter, so that fear would not stop the מצוה.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
his heart will strike him and he will separate.
phrases.notes: He means the groom would be so scared he might stay away entirely and never complete the marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לו אם כן לבו נוקפו ופורש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reasoning: a stricter rule would backfire
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A pious man should stop before finishing, to be extra careful.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a rule would cause fear and make him avoid the מצוה, so it was not made.

steps.title: Continuous bleeding past the allowed time requires examination
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches: if the bleeding keeps flowing past the time she is given (four nights, or one night), she cannot assume it is דם בתולים. She must examine herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: All of these women who were discharging blood continually, from within the four nights to after the four nights, or from within the one night to after that night, must all examine themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא that explains the משנה's time limits for the bride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives some brides four nights and others one night, during which blood is assumed to be דם בתולים. The ברייתא adds that if the bleeding flows on past that limit, this assumption no longer holds. She must check herself.

keyTerms.meaning: Four nights, the time the משנה gives some brides
Blood from the torn hymen, which is pure

steps.confusionAlert: 'From within four nights to after four nights' means one continuous flow that starts during the allowed time and goes past it. It does not mean new bleeding that starts later.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
And all of them who were discharging blood continually,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the brides listed in the משנה, each with her allowed time.

phrases.aramaic: מִתּוֹךְ אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת לְאַחַר אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת,
phrases.english: from within four nights to after four nights,
from within the night to after the night —
all of them must examine themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן וכולן שהיו שופעות דם ובאות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'acts and separates' discussion and returns to explaining the משנה's time limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bleeding that continues past the allowed time is not automatically treated as דם בתולים. The woman must examine herself.

steps.title: רבי מאיר is strict like בית שמאי in all these cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that in all these cases, רבי מאיר follows the stricter view of בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in all of them, רבי מאיר is strict, following the words of בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and tells us which side of the משנה's argument רבי מאיר follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי give a minor bride four nights, while בית הלל allow her until the wound heals. רבי מאיר takes the stricter view in all the cases. So once the allowed time is over, the woman must examine herself.

keyTerms.meaning: And in all of them, meaning in all the cases listed

steps.whatToRemember: The allowed time (four nights, or one night) is a firm limit. Bleeding after it must be checked, and רבי מאיר is strict like בית שמאי in all cases.

phrases.english: And in all of them,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר מַחְמִיר כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir is stringent in accordance with the words of Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: ובכולן רבי מאיר מחמיר כדברי בית שמאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא by giving רבי מאיר's position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In all these cases, רבי מאיר follows בית שמאי's stricter limits.

steps.title: In the other cases, look at the blood's appearance
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that in the other cases where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue, רבי מאיר says to judge by how the blood looks.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the other cases of seeing blood where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue, follow how the blood looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from Step 27 and limits it. In the other cases where the two houses argue, רבי מאיר does not simply follow the strict view. He says to look at the blood's appearance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said רבי מאיר follows the strict view of בית שמאי. Here we learn that this is not true in every case. In the other disputes, the blood's appearance decides whether it is נדה blood or בתולים blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The other cases of seeing blood

phrases.english: And the other cases of seeing blood
that are disputed between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
follow the appearance of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר רְאִיּוֹת שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits Step 27's statement that רבי מאיר follows בית שמאי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the remaining disputes, רבי מאיר decides by the appearance of the blood.

steps.title: רבי מאיר explains how the two kinds of blood differ
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that נדה blood and בתולים blood are different in color, clearness, and where they come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to say: the two kinds of blood look different from each other. How? נדה blood is red, and בתולים blood is not red. נדה blood is cloudy, and בתולים blood is not cloudy. נדה blood comes from the womb, and בתולים blood comes from the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason for the rule in Step 28. It shows how one can tell the two kinds of blood apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood looks different, then checking its appearance makes sense. רבי מאיר lists three differences: color, clearness, and source. That is why he can say 'follow the appearance of the blood.'

keyTerms.meaning: Menstrual blood, which makes her טמאה

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי מאיר thinks the blood's appearance can decide whether she is טהורה or טמאה.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: מַרְאֵה דָמִים מְשׁוּנִּים הֵן זֶה מִזֶּה
phrases.english: The appearances of blood are different from one another.
How so?
The blood of a niddah is red;
virginal blood is not red.
The blood of a niddah is cloudy;
virginal blood is not cloudy.
The blood of a niddah comes from the source;
virginal blood comes from the sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind Step 28's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נדה blood and בתולים blood can be told apart by color, clearness, and source.

steps.title: The חכמים hold that all blood looks the same
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the idea of telling the bloods apart is only רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say all blood looks the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר רבי יוסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this is רבי מאיר's view. But the חכמים say all appearances of blood are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא tells us that רבי מאיר's idea is not agreed on by everyone. The חכמים disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, you cannot tell נדה blood from בתולים blood by looking at it. So for them, the appearance of the blood cannot decide anything here.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion against רבי מאיר
They are all one, the same

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says you can tell the bloods apart by appearance. The חכמים say all blood looks the same.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Rabbi Yosei said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
but the Sages say:
All appearances of blood are one.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that Step 29's idea is only one opinion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים hold that all blood looks the same, so appearance cannot tell them apart.

steps.title: A woman who bleeds from marital relations three times
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a woman who bleeds because of marital relations may continue the first, second, and third time. After that, she may not continue until she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a woman who sees blood because of marital relations may have relations the first, second, and third time. From then on, she may not have relations until she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It is about a woman who bleeds every time she is with her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bleeding once or twice could be chance, so she may continue up to the third time. After three times it is clearly a pattern, so she may not continue with this husband. The rule is that she may not have relations until she is divorced.
steps.confusionAlert: Three times is the limit. She may still have relations up to the third time, and the ban only starts after that.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A woman who sees blood because of relations
may have relations the first time,
and the second, and the third.
From here on,
she may not have relations until she is divorced

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאָה דָּם מֵחֲמַת תַּשְׁמִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of בתולים blood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After bleeding from relations three times, she may not have relations with her husband until she is divorced.
